# photographie-web

Ce skill possède le choix des images d'un site, leurs licences et les fichiers maîtres remis.
Une mauvaise photo peut ruiner un design [3918934 S10 Image d'illustration R70].

## Quand charger

- Un site a besoin de photos.
- Avant de briefer une séance photo.
- Avant de briefer un achat en banque d'images.
- Avant de briefer une retouche.
- Avant d'accepter des images pour le site.

## Faire

### 1. Cadrer le besoin

1. Demander au client le but des photos et le message pour ses clients cibles, avant de choisir props et fonds [4044684 S4 P59].
2. Photo produit : plus de ventes, meilleure expérience client, moins de retours [4044684 S1 P1].
3. Image réelle et attrayante, car l'acheteur ne touche pas le produit [4044684 S1 P2-P3].
4. Lister les types : produit, narratives (« les plus importantes »), illustrations, motifs avec modération [437398 S5 WDR#3 R59].

### 2. Choisir la source

1. La voie d'image se tranche au début du projet, avant toute proposition visuelle, selon la situation [décision du capitaine, 11 novembre 2026] :
   - une séance photo, quand il y a quelque chose de beau à montrer et un budget ;
   - une banque d'images, choisie comme une série cohérente ;
   - un site sans photo, porté par la couleur, la typographie et le dessin, quand il n'y a rien à photographier.
2. La banque est gratuite pour le moment, sous une licence qui permet l'usage commercial sans achat ; la banque payante est à revoir plus tard [décision du capitaine, 11 novembre 2026].
   Autre position : selon le budget, ses photos, un photographe dirigé par vous, la bibliothèque du client (meilleur cas), le stock payant, le stock gratuit en dernier recours [3543948 Bonus › Setting Rules for Photos R142] ; retenue la décision du capitaine pour la banque, l'ordre du cours valant pour les autres sources.
3. En banque, un stock authentique, jamais générique ni surproduit [437398 S5 WDR#3 R60].
4. Chaque image de banque est relevée : page d'origine, auteur, licence, emplacement dans le site [décision du capitaine, 11 novembre 2026].
5. Toute source payante remonte au capitaine avant le brief [3918934 R69] [autorité firstmate].

### 3. Fixer les règles photo du site

1. Décrire les photos qui portent le message et le ton [3543948 Bonus › Setting Rules for Photos R141].
2. Sincérité : l'image de banque donne l'ambiance, la photo du client prouve [décision du capitaine, 11 novembre 2026].
3. Une image de banque ne se fait jamais passer pour le produit, le lieu ou les personnes du client, ni par sa place ni par sa légende [décision du capitaine, 11 novembre 2026].
4. Les petites photos du client, prises par lui et de qualité modeste, servent de preuve, en petit, jamais agrandies au-delà de leur taille réelle ; les photos d'une séance commandée restent de grandes images, retouchées selon l'étape 6 [décision du capitaine, 11 novembre 2026].
5. Nommer trois caractéristiques de choix [3543948 R144].
6. Bibliothèque fixe et règle de quantité par design [3543948 P22, R143] : une grande image par écran, les petites photos du client en preuve à côté [décision du capitaine, 11 novembre 2026].
   Autre position : deux photos au plus par design, au-delà le point focal se perd [3543948 P22] ; retenue la décision du capitaine, éprouvée à l'essai, où la grande image garde le point focal.
7. Ne pas mélanger les styles de photos [3918934 S10 Image d'illustration R68].
8. En banque, des séries du même photographe [412738 L86 P353].
9. Les couleurs des photos suivent la palette du site ; l'autre issue, un site réduit à un neutre et un petit accent, relève de `design-visuel` [5313020 L31].

### 4. Briefer une séance

Le brief contient :

1. Un plan écrit et une liste de plans [4044684 S5 P88].
2. Une planche d'inspiration de 5 à 7 références, sans copie [4044684 S6 P90].
3. Un thème de 1 à 3 adjectifs [4044684 S5 P92].
4. Deux à trois couleurs, 2 à 3 props par scène, chacun utile [4044684 S5 P96, P98, P99].
5. Une seule source de lumière, jamais de lumières mêlées [4044684 S3 P42].
6. Un produit propre [4044684 S5 P103].
7. Le format paysage pour un site [4044684 S4 P77], de l'espace pour un texte [4044684 S4 P78] [préférence].
8. Produit sur fond propre et narratif en situation [437398 S5 WDR#3 R59] ; 1595266 S6/L39 P273 préfère la situation réelle.
9. Le flash pour les gros produits [4044684 S3 P54].

Pour le produit :

1. « Le blanc doit être blanc » [4044684 S3 P48], bords blanc pur pour un site blanc [2633036 Prod/Modifier P110].
2. Lignes droites [4044684 S10 P82].
3. Faible profondeur de champ [4044684 S2 P17] ; 2633036 Prod Pr12 ferme à f/8-f/11.

Pour une personne :

1. Le visage en point focal [412738 L87 P366], net aux yeux [2633036 Focus/Manuel vs AF P37].
2. Le visage dit la personnalité, le corps le physique [412738 L77 P270].
3. Lumière douce : ciel couvert, heure dorée, fenêtre [2633036 Écl P60, P62].
4. Fond sans distraction ; varier les plans [2633036 Compo P32, Portr/Conseils P101].

Fichiers maîtres :

1. RAW [4044684 S2 P11, 2633036 Anat/RAW vs JPEG P42] ; 4044684 S8 P12 s'en passe sur iPhone pour les réseaux.
2. sRGB à la prise de vue [4044684 S2 P14].
3. Un dossier daté par produit [4044684 S8 P129].

### 5. Briefer un achat en banque d'images

1. La liste « Choisir une image » [1595266 S6/L39] :
   1. La référence est-elle précise ? Personne réelle si oui, illustration sinon.
   2. Produit précis ? Montrer le produit (captures d'écran pour un logiciel), pas une métaphore générique.
   3. L'image raconte-t-elle une histoire réaliste, peu posée, où l'on se projette ?
   4. A-t-elle un point focal clair (couleur, composition) et peu d'éléments ?
   5. Communique-t-elle le concept d'un coup d'œil ?
   6. Montre-t-elle produit et personnes en situation réelle, avec une tonalité adaptée (chaude plutôt que froide et pâle) ?
2. Rarement exclusives : le concurrent peut avoir la même [3918934 S10 Image d'illustration R72].
3. Respecter la licence, crédit compris [3918934 R72].

### 6. Briefer une retouche

1. Simple et subtile : « on ne voit pas la différence mais on la sent » [4044684 S8 P124].
2. Non destructive, original intact [2633036 PS P130, 4044684 S6 P134].
3. Vibrance plutôt que saturation [2633036 PS/Couleur P132, 4044684 S8 P126].
4. Portrait : yeux un peu éclaircis, peau un peu adoucie [2633036 PS/Session portrait P140].
5. Garder grains de beauté et signes durables [2633036 PS P139] [préférence].
6. Réglages copiés sur la série, sans le recadrage [4044684 S8 P128].
7. Produit, dans l'ordre : recadrer et redresser ; balance des blancs sur le fond ; blancs +, hautes lumières -, ombres -, noirs - ; saturation légère ; correcteur ; courbe ; accentuation ; vignette blanche [2633036 Prod/Modifier Pr13].

### 7. Accepter les images

1. Une image floue ou très sous-exposée ne se récupère pas [4044684 S10 P34].
2. Histogramme sans pic collé à un bord, sauf effet voulu [2633036 Expo P21, 4044684 S2 P23-P24].
3. Revue d'un résultat raté : lumière ? composition ? déséquilibre ? props trop grands ou couleurs distrayantes ? angle ? image pas droite ? [4044684 S7 P143].
4. Rien posé sur un visage [3543948 Bonus › Part 3 R145].
5. Série conforme aux règles photo du site [3918934 R68], sincérité comprise, relevé à l'appui [décision du capitaine, 11 novembre 2026].
6. Pas de filigrane [4044684 S8 P132] [préférence] ; 2633036 LrC P149 le dit utile [préférence].
7. Licence vérifiée [3918934 R72, 2633036 P186].
8. RAW et originaux intacts remis [4044684 S2 P11, S6 P134].

## Refuser ou remonter

**Capitaine**

- Le budget photo et qui le paie : séance sur le devis, banque payée par le client [3918934 S10 Image d'illustration R69, R71, R72].
- L'engagement d'un photographe, à la charge du client [3918934 R73] [autorité firstmate].
- Un doute sur un droit d'usage : permission et avocat [2633036 Stock/Licences P186].

**Firstmate**

- La source, budget validé [autorité firstmate].
- Les règles photo et la liste de plans [autorité firstmate].
- L'acceptation des images livrées [autorité firstmate].

**Worker**

- Les réglages de retouche, dans l'étape 6 [autorité firstmate].
- Le choix entre images qui passent l'étape 5 [autorité firstmate].

**Refus nets**

- Pas d'image générée pour un vrai produit : l'IA améliore l'existant, la vraie photo inspire confiance [4044684 S6 P134-P137, P139].
- Pas d'image sans licence : « libre de droits » ne veut pas dire gratuit [2633036 Stock/Licences P186, 3918934 R72].
- Pas de stock mis en scène ni de métaphore littérale [1595266 S6/L39 P266, P268].

## Références

Cours sources :

- 2633036 Photography Masterclass : Expo, Compo, Focus, Anat (RAW), Écl, Portr, Prod, PS, Stock.
- 4044684 Product Photography for All : S1 à S8, S10.
- 1595266 Design Rules: Visual Design Principles for Great UI Design : S6/L39.
- 3543948 The Branding Masterclass : Bonus › Setting Rules for Photos, Bonus › Part 3.
- 3918934 Fondamentaux du webdesign : S10 Image d'illustration.
- 412738 UX & Web Design Master Course: Strategy, Design, Development : L77, L86, L87.
- 437398 Build Responsive Real-World Websites with HTML and CSS : S5 WDR#3.
- 5313020 the color class : L31.

Frontières :

- Les formats, poids, dimensions et réglages d'export relèvent de `performance-web`.
- Le texte alternatif relève de `accessibilite`.
- Le texte posé sur une image relève de `design-visuel`.
- Les fichiers du logo et la palette de marque relèvent de `identite-marque-logo`.
- Le devis, le contrat et ses livrables relèvent de `agence-projet-client`.

commands.name: caveman
commands.description: Terse caveman voice: answer first, fluff gone, every technical fact kept. Use for /caveman, "caveman mode", "talk like caveman", "be brief", "less tokens". Stays on until "stop caveman" or "normal mode". (user)

commands.name: lavish
commands.description: Turn complex or visual agent responses into rich, reviewable HTML artifacts (HTML files) the user can annotate and send feedback on, using the lavish-axi CLI. Use when about to give a plan, comparison, diagram, table, code diff, report, or anything easier to grasp visually than as prose. (user)

commands.name: no-mistakes
commands.description: Validate your code changes through the no-mistakes pipeline - automated code review, tests, lint, docs, push, PR, and CI - before they reach the configured push target. Use when the user asks to run no-mistakes, gate or ship or validate their changes, push safely, asks you to do a task and then validate it, or invokes /no-mistakes. (user)

commands.name: ponytail
commands.description: Forces the laziest solution that actually works, simplest, shortest, most minimal. Channels a senior dev who has seen everything: question whether the task needs to exist at all (YAGNI), reach for the standard library before custom code, native platform features before dependencies, one line before fifty. Supports intensity levels: lite, full (default), ultra. Use on ANY coding task: writing, adding, refactoring, fixing, reviewing, or designing code, and choosing libraries or dependencies. Also use whenever the user says "ponytail", "be lazy", "lazy mode", "simplest solution", "minimal solution", "yagni", "do less", or "shortest path", or complains about over-engineering, bloat, boilerplate, or unnecessary dependencies. Do NOT use for non-coding requests (general knowledge, prose, translation, summaries, recipes). (user)

commands.name: rtk
commands.description: Use RTK (Rust Token Killer) to compress verbose shell output (git, tests, linters, builds, gh, docker, find, grep) before it enters context. Use for rtk, token savings, or before noisy CLI commands. (user)

commands.name: afk
commands.description: Enter the away posture when the captain invokes /afk, says they are going afk, `state/.afk-contract` or `state/.afk` exists, an incoming message starts with `FM_INJECT_MARK`, or any `state/.subsuper-*` marker is involved. Load it at once in the /afk turn, before any other work, and on the first unmarked message while away to render the return brief. (project)

commands.name: ahoy
commands.description: Recap visible session events and guide the captain through visibly unanswered decisions when the captain explicitly invokes /ahoy, with a Bearings fallback when /ahoy is the session's first real captain message. (project)

commands.name: bearings
commands.description: Generate a "pick up where I left off" fleet digest. Use when the captain invokes /bearings (plain, file, or lavish) or asks for a bearings report, morning brief, status report, catch-up, "where did I leave off", or "what's in the works". Also use on a contributions check wake, when filing work linked to an upstream issue, and on a procevent lavish wake whose source id is the bearings board's. (project)

commands.name: quiet
commands.description: Enter quiet supervision mode when the captain invokes /quiet or asks for quiet mode, quiet-while-present, or fewer routine wake turns while they stay in the session. Unlike /afk, ordinary captain chat does not exit it; only an explicit `/quiet off` does. (project)

commands.name: stow
commands.description: Sweep the session for uncaptured durable knowledge and unfiled or wrong open work records, and curate startup memory. Use when the captain invokes /stow (e.g. "/stow", "stow what you've learned"), before a session reset or context compaction, or periodically to keep operational memory current. (project)

commands.name: updatefirstmate
commands.description: Self-update a running firstmate and its secondmates to the latest from origin, or from a configured self-update source. Use when the captain invokes /updatefirstmate (e.g. "/updatefirstmate", "update firstmate", "pull the latest firstmate"). (project)

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's recipe covers them) at the effort level given first, before any target (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings to many, some uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply them to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: schedule
commands.description: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator
commands.description: Author or improve the run-<unit> skill - a per-project skill that tells agents how to build, launch, and drive this project's app. Use when the user asks to set up the project, get it running, write run instructions, or verify build/run steps work from a clean environment.

commands.description: Make a mod: a change to Claude's own interface or behaviour, such as a panel or pane that stays beside the chat and updates, a band, status line, toast, slash command, or hook on tool calls. Use to make, change or debug a mod or its hooks module.

commands.name: built-in-browser
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: chrome-browser
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. commands.description: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: google-workspace
commands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: graphify
commands.description: Turn a folder, repo or files (code, docs, PDFs, images) into a queryable knowledge graph with interactive HTML and a report. Use for /graphify, map this codebase, knowledge graph, or questions when graphify-out/ exists. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: import-memory
commands.description: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: morning
commands.description: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pdf
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: anthropic-skills:ponytail
commands.description: Lazy senior dev mode: smallest complete change, reuse before writing. Use on any coding task, or when the user says ponytail, be lazy, simplest solution, yagni, or complains about bloat. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: ponytail-audit
commands.description: Quality audit of a whole repo: bugs, security, load, untested risky code, slow paths, what to delete or merge. Ranked report, changes nothing. Use for audit this codebase, review the whole repo, find bloat, /ponytail-audit. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: ponytail-debt
commands.description: List every shortcut: comment (and older ponytail: ones) as a debt ledger. One-shot report, changes nothing. Use for ponytail debt, what did ponytail defer, list the shortcuts, /ponytail-debt. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: ponytail-gain
commands.description: Show ponytail's measured savings (code, cost, speed) from its published benchmark. One-shot display. Use for /ponytail-gain, what does ponytail save, ponytail impact. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: ponytail-help
commands.description: Quick reference for ponytail levels and skills. One-shot display. Use for /ponytail-help, ponytail help, how do I use ponytail. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: ponytail-review
commands.description: Quality review of a change: logic, safety, load, tests, speed, and whether every line is needed. Use for review this, code review, review the last commit, review my PR, is this over-engineered, /ponytail-review. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pptx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: skill-creator
commands.description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved. (claude.ai sync)

commands.description: See how real apps handle a flow (onboarding, sign-up, checkout, paywall, settings...) before designing it.

commands.name: claude.ai UXKIN:find_design_system (MCP)
commands.description: Find real website design systems that fit a product and mood, with their DESIGN.md.

commands.name: claude.ai UXKIN:review_my_ui (MCP)
commands.description: Review a screen or page in this project against how real products do the same thing, and suggest fixes.

commands.name: claude.ai UXKIN:build_from_collection (MCP)
commands.description: Use references you saved on UXKIN as the starting point for what you build next.

commands.description: Prompt template for analyzing website performance over a specified time period. Returns structured messages for LLM-driven performance insights and optimization recommendations.

content.text:
Captain, voici le verdict pour chaque cas, d'après le seul texte du skill `photographie-web`.

| Cas | Verdict | Règle principale |
|---|---|---|
| a | PERMIS (sous condition) | « Fixer les règles photo du site », règles 2 et 3 |
| b | INTERDIT | « Fixer les règles photo du site », règle 3 |
| c | INTERDIT | « Fixer les règles photo du site », règle 4 |
| d | PERMIS | « Fixer les règles photo du site », règle 4 |
| e | PERMIS | « Fixer les règles photo du site », règle 4 |
| f | INTERDIT | « Choisir la source », règle 5 |
| g | INTERDIT | « Choisir la source », règle 4 |

**a. PERMIS, sous condition.**
- Section 3, règle 2 : « l'image de banque donne l'ambiance », ce qui est exactement son rôle ici.
- Section 3, règle 6 : une grande image par écran est admise.
- Condition, section 3, règle 3 : l'image ne doit pas passer pour un chantier du client, « ni par sa place ni par sa légende ». Sans légende et en ambiance d'accueil, elle passe ; placée dans une rubrique de réalisations, elle deviendrait interdite. C'est ma lecture, le skill ne tranche pas ce cas mot pour mot.
- Section 2, règle 3 : le stock doit rester authentique, ni générique ni surproduit.
- Le titre posé sur l'image relève de `design-visuel` (Références, Frontières).

**b. INTERDIT.**
- Section 3, règle 3 : une image de banque ne se fait jamais passer pour les personnes du client, et la légende « Marc, notre fondateur » fait précisément cela.
- Section 3, règle 2 : c'est la photo du client qui prouve, pas la banque.
- Section 5, règle 1, point 1 : pour une référence précise, il faut la personne réelle.

**c. INTERDIT.**
- Section 3, règle 4 : les petites photos du client ne sont « jamais agrandies au-delà de leur taille réelle ». Une image de 640 px en plein écran enfreint cette règle.

**d. PERMIS.**
- Section 3, règle 4 : ces photos « servent de preuve, en petit ».
- Section 3, règle 6 : « les petites photos du client en preuve à côté ».
- Section 3, règle 2 : la photo du client prouve.

**e. PERMIS.**
- Section 3, règle 4 : « les photos d'une séance commandée restent de grandes images, retouchées selon l'étape 6 ».
- Section 2, règle 1 : la séance photo est une des trois voies possibles, tranchée au début du projet.
- La retouche doit suivre la section 6, notamment la règle 1 (simple et subtile) et la règle 2 (non destructive, original intact).

**f. INTERDIT.**
- Section 2, règle 5 : « toute source payante remonte au capitaine avant le brief ».
- Section 2, règle 2 : la banque est gratuite pour le moment, la banque payante est à revoir plus tard.
- « Refuser ou remonter », Capitaine, 1er point : le budget photo et qui le paie relèvent du capitaine.
- « Refuser ou remonter », Worker, 2e point : le worker ne décide que du choix entre images qui passent l'étape 5, pas d'un achat.

**g. INTERDIT.**
- Section 2, règle 4 : chaque image de banque est relevée avec page d'origine, auteur, licence et emplacement dans le site.
- Section 7, règle 5 : l'acceptation se fait « relevé à l'appui ».
- Section 7, règle 7 : la licence doit être vérifiée.
- Section 5, règle 3 : respecter la licence, crédit compris, ce qui est impossible sans auteur connu.
- « Refuser ou remonter », Refus nets, 2e point : pas d'image sans licence.

Aucun script n'a été exécuté et aucun worker lancé ; seul le skill a été chargé.
